label: The byte baseline any fail-loud drift guard would compare against is exact but single-template: the seeder-semantics check (qq{} block with real newlines matched as a literal, mirroring the perl's quoted block) matches core/spec.md.tmpl exactly and no-matches the phase-parent, research and review packet-type templates. Phase parents scaffold from the lean template whose [Trigger phrase 1]/[Trigger phrase 2] placeholders never reach the substitution (the guard requires the core phrase), have no replacer anywhere in the CLI tree, and are pinned as retained by the golden snapshot; two live packets carry the placeholder and the committed index contains the normalized phrase, so the placeholders enter the index as real search phrases while the judge's template-default class holds only the four core phrases. Direction: seed the parent placeholders at render time or add the bracket literals to the template-default class, updating the golden snapshot deliberately.

The index-freshness cadence has a mechanical detector in CI and it is report-only end to end: advisory-checks.yml runs generate-trigger-index.mjs --check on every PR and on pushes to main/skilled/** with continue-on-error and a fallback echo, failing closed only when the generator file is missing; no workflow regenerates the artifact, and trigger-index.vitest.ts covers parser, encoding, scoring and the judge's template-default rejection but has no manifest-freshness assertion. Drift is therefore detectable on every PR and repaired never automatically; the actionable choice is to promote the step to gating or pair the report with a maintainer regeneration lane.

The advisory-only boundary is precisely test-mapped: create-track-refresh.vitest.ts pins the lister's stderr format, 14-day window, phase-child silence, single-JSON stdout and status 0, and pins the track-root refresh path's warn-and-continue on unreadable metadata and missing writer; the lister's own failure returns and the seeder's status are pinned by no test. A deterministic seeder drift guard that stays silent on healthy fixtures is therefore collision-free with this suite (fixtures scaffold from the real templates), while fail-loud changes to the refresh path or to the listing format must update the pins, and any phase-parent seeding change must update the golden snapshot.

Any template-drift comparison must reproduce the seeder's construction: build the block with qq{} (real newlines) and match it as a literal, as the \Q$block\E substitution does. An inline regex carrying backslash-n inside a quoted block quotes the backslash-n literally and reports NO-MATCH against core/spec.md.tmpl, which the literal form demonstrably matches; an inline-pattern guard is a false-negative generator and must also cover all four phrases, not the one the shell guard greps.
